Eltikan (Eltikan, G60)

Region (English scoring-table region): South Aelantir.

In brief: Unite a tribal kingdom in western Aelantir, use boar cavalry, subject integration, and bronze artificery to prove yourself to the cities of Kiohesh, then decide how Taychend's future will be arranged.

Narrative: Very high | Mission-tree length: Long (44 direct G60 missions; related files contain missions unavailable to this country) | Mission-tree update: Use the local script supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: Very high | Waiting: Medium-high (proof-of-war and expedition prerequisites) | Early pressure: High | Expansion capacity: High

A Kingdom of Unifiers

Eltikan is not a one-city restoration project in 1444. The local history gives G60 extensive holdings in western Aelantir, Eltibhar culture, Gotiriei faith, and the Tribal Kingdom reform; its capital is province 2785. The history records Aosiki, called “the Righteous Uniter,” and treats the nearby Kheionai powers as threats. The fixed English Wiki adds that Fasíri tribes had long competed for the title of divinely appointed unifier; Aosiki gathered them together in the first half of the fifteenth century and proclaimed the kingdom in 1440. Its later conquest, succession crisis, and collapse in 1476 belong to the world's chronicle, not an irreversible player opening. [Local historical script] [Wiki material]

The Wiki also describes an older pastoral society, boar mounts, bronze craft, and longstanding hostility toward the eastern cities. The current cavalry and tribal mechanics fit that background, but the encyclopedia does not turn every ancient raid in the Wiki into a scripted mission. The practical question is how a ruler who has united the western peoples can cross Kheionai alliance networks and turn military victory into durable governance. [Wiki material] [Local scripts]

In the fixed Wiki history Aosiki later took Lokemeion, died in 1473 while fighting the eastern city-states, and left a succession crisis that broke the kingdom apart in 1476. This explains why the mission tree stresses institutions that can survive a ruler, but it is not a countdown imposed on every save. Current missions can redirect the ending toward coexistence with cities, magical industry, or a Taychend dual empire; the Wiki line is not an inevitable failure. [Wiki material] [Local scripts]

Opening the Cities Through Subjects

The early dedicated missions can advance through direct conquest or by making neighbours subjects and integrating them later. This subject-to-inheritance rhythm differs from simply eating land: the player first creates obedience relationships and manages urban elites, then gains the possibility of rapid map consolidation. For Kheionai residents, later missions offer land rights, shared festivals, and participation by city advisers; these choices have coexistence and public-building aspects while also legitimising the new kingdom's rule over conquered cities. [Local scripts] [Local narrative text]

Boar cavalry, bronze equipment, and mountain operations give the opening war a clear identity, but they also create high pressure. Player posts repeatedly discuss an early pilgrimage and the window before neighbouring alliances close; those are version-specific experiences, not mandatory current triggers. If the opening diplomatic network cannot be broken, even a country larger than many one-province states can lose its first war. Once the city region is entered, Eltikan must also pay the costs of tax, roads, production, and religious integration. [Local scripts] [Community views]

The promise of city integration needs qualification. Granting nobles land rights and admitting advisers can reduce the friction of purely military occupation and help ordinary residents avoid prolonged war, but the text still expects the conquered to accept Eltibhar culture and faith. Coexistence and assimilation are interwoven; this is not unconditional equality, and a city festival is not proof that residents freely chose the new political order. [Local narrative text]

Magic Forges and the Taychend Fork

The middle missions turn mages from a court privilege into part of national industry and the army. New magic, magical forges, and special alloys require a sufficiently loyal mage estate, investment, and high-production provinces; war wizards require manpower, military resources, and money. This is not free opening strength. It teaches a bronze tribe to maintain cross-regional supply and complex manufacture, then extends the campaign toward Amadia and Taychend far beyond the original western mountains. [Local scripts]

The ending event must not be misread. One option gives Taychend land to a specified subject, creates a “dual empire” subject relationship, and changes that subject into J84, the Taychend Empire. The other option has Eltikan inherit that subject while keeping G60. The current event proves that G60 can control J84's creation; it does not prove an automatic G60-to-J84 change. The separate Taychendi Empire (J84) encyclopedia article remains the source boundary for that country and is not duplicated as a direct G60 mission. [Local scripts]

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansionism 88/100 | Autocracy 76/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 58/100 (100 = Magic, 0 = Artifice; theme intensity 74/100) | Pluralism 58/100. Phase profile: western tribal unification (theme intensity 35, pluralism 38) → Kheionai and Taychend integration (theme intensity 74, pluralism 65).

The v2.1 value score is Neutral (65/100), with an improving trajectory. Phase scores move from tribal conquest and proof of war (Neutral, 50/100) toward land rights and shared-festival integration (Good, 70/100). Land rights for city residents, shared festivals, city rebuilding, and cross-cultural representation are substantive positive evidence; forced subject relations, destructive language toward political opponents, and military proof of legitimacy limit restraint. The representative missions do not establish systematic extermination. The Chinese source repeats the phase comparison here: tribal conquest and proof of war (Neutral, 50/100) → land rights and shared-festival integration (Good, 70/100). Its accompanying explanation credits land rights, shared festivals, city rebuilding, and sharing achievements across peoples, while military legitimacy, forced subject relations, and destructive language toward political opponents limit restraint. The representative missions do not directly establish slavery, human sacrifice, or systematic extermination, so conquest of city-states alone is not grounds for an Evil classification. It suits players who enjoy an aggressive opening, subject integration, bronze cavalry, and a long transition into magical industry; avoid it if you want quiet internal development or low early-war pressure. [Local scripts] [Local narrative text]

A 2024 player thread raises early mission-condition and pilgrimage-opening problems, including developer discussion and an old repair plan. It helps identify likely friction but cannot prove that the same bug remains in v1.37.5.0. See the source receipt. [Community views]

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces native English national-idea names and descriptions alongside the inherited source displays. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Successor ideas do not stack automatically with the predecessor set. Descriptions may recount history or depict a future ideal, not events already completed in 1444. Native English prose is used rather than back-translating the Chinese localisation; any inherited display/unit uncertainty remains unresolved.

Eltikan (G60) — Eltibhar Ideas

Traditions: Eltibhar Traditions

Effects: global_regiment_cost：-10%; National tax modifier: +15%.

Idea 1: A Hardy Land, A Hardy People

The western side of the island known to outsiders as Alecand is not an easy place to live. While the mountains shield us from most of the worst of the death winds, meaning we do not have to suffer the way those in the east do, our soil is still barren and rocky. However, this has taught us one thing: only the strongest and most resourceful survive, so in our raids against the easterners and each other, we will make sure we exploit the land to the fullest.

Effects: Reinforce speed: +10%.

Idea 2: Cyclopean Masonry

Our forts are not constructed in the style typical to elsewhere; since we do not have easy means to shear rock or make mortar ourselves, we have learned to solve the puzzle of the boulders directly. In other words, our walls are made from boulders carefully stacked together to pack tightly even without extra reinforcement. This makes our architecture not only imposing, but surprisingly sturdy.

Effects: Build time: -10%; Fort maintenance: -10%.

Idea 3: Masters of Bronze

On our island, the only sources of iron are within the territories of the easterners' cities. This has meant we lack a proper ironworking tradition. What we do have, however, is copper, and lots of it. From this we can forge bronze, and thanks to our long tradition of working with it as well as having to make sure it can compete with eastern metallurgic developments, means our bronze is stronger than any one might find elsewhere.

Effects: fire_damage_received：-10%.

Idea 4: Ghílti Kanvrenu

Since time immemorial our people have gotten together to compete against each other in brotherhood. When we weren't raiding each other before unification, we would come together in great festivals to show off our martial prowess to each other. It has been suggested that we formalize these festivals, known as the Ghílti Kanvrenu in our language, and hold one every year so that our greatest warriors and strategists can be shown off for all to see.

Effects: Military advisor cost: -25%.

Idea 5: Crowning the First Riei

It was a solemn affair. The greatest generals and nobles of our nation were lined up in the best finery. Our priests practiced their holiest rites. And at the center of it all, our chieftain. But as the crown fell on their head, they were no longer just a mere chieftain: they were now the first king, Riei, of all the Eltikani people.

Effects: Legitimacy: +1; Devotion: +1; Republican tradition: +0.3; Horde unity: +1.

Idea 6: The Holy Mountain

Rigòti, the greatest peak on our island. Our holy protector from the winds of death. So ubiquitous and quintessential to everyone's way of life, the easterners simply call it Meteí, ‘The Mountain', for it needs no other name. For eons our people have climbed this mountain to seek holy wisdom and enlightenment from its embrace. At the urging of our priests, we will establish waystations along the disparate paths up its cliffs and valleys to ensure all of our people who wish to may glimpse even a fragment of the divine.

Effects: Clergy loyalty equilibrium: +10%; True faith tolerance: +2.

Idea 7: Code Talkers

As we have begun to engage in contact with the outside world, we have started to realize something: nobody else speaks quite like we do. Even those from the eastern shores have extreme difficulty understanding our sentences. While this does mean many foreign diplomats dread being assigned to our court and having to master our way of speaking, the same also applies to their spies, making it easier for us to make sure that things we want to be secret, stay secret.

Effects: global_spy_defence：+20%.

Ambition: Eltibhar Ambition

Effects: Cavalry combat ability: +15%.
